novelty.justification: The claim proposes a measurement/application combination: “Reasoning steps decompose into a sparse dictionary of interpretable operation-features” and some such features have “activation [that] predicts prunable reasoning.” Searches for “sparse autoencoder chain-of-thought reasoning operations,” “step-level SAE reasoning,” and “SAE redundant reasoning pruning” identify the closest work as Step-Level Sparse Autoencoder for Reasoning Process Interpretation (2026), How does Chain of Thought Think? (2025), and, on redundancy removal, Making Slow Thinking Faster (2025) and Causal Sufficiency and Necessity Improves Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (2025). Moving from SAE features for CoT/step properties plus established step-pruning methods to an operation-feature taxonomy whose redundancy features guide pruning is a natural but non-trivial integration, not a wholly new core interpretability paradigm; the specific operation-to-prunability relationship appears differentiated, supporting standard rather than high novelty.
